latin: Magnus aquilo fons est animarum omnium simpliciter, sicut alu dies quarundam et non omnium.
latin_note: Farmer's transcription reads 'alu dies'; Wirszubski's own quotation of the same conclusio (his 'Conclusio VI') reads 'alii dies' at both of its occurrences (wirszubski1989:1479, 1482), which is followed here as the evidently correct reading of an OCR-damaged word in Farmer's copy-text.
translation: The great North is the source of all souls absolutely, just as other 'days' are [the source] of some, and not of all.
translation_note: 'Aquilo' (the north wind/the North) and 'dies' ('days') are technical terms of a Kabbalistic scheme of the emanation of souls, on which Farmer directs comparison to Scholem (farmer1998:17661); 'quarundam' (feminine genitive plural, 'of some [souls]') is understood to govern 'animarum' carried over from the first clause.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch7, from Latin at farmer1998:17637
doctrine: Farmer directs the reader to Scholem's discussion of the emanation of souls in the Kabbalah for the doctrine's background, glossing 'dies' simply as 'days' (farmer1998:17661). Wirszubski identifies the thesis as his 'Conclusio VI' and begins an analysis by stating that 'the interpretation of this thesis depends entirely on the precise location of' [the referent], though the material consulted breaks off before giving his conclusion (wirszubski1989:1482).
context: Farmer's cross-reference network links the thesis to two Cabalistic (own-opinion) conclusions confirming the Christian religion that likewise invoke 'Aquilo' (11>37 at farmer1998:27217, 11>47 at farmer1998:27343), and to 28.8 in the same Hebrew Cabalists section, on souls descending from the third light to the fourth and fifth days (farmer1998:17645).
historiography: Wirszubski (1989) transcribes and numbers this conclusio ('Conclusio VI') and opens a discussion of its interpretation turning on 'the precise location' of a referent in the text, which the material consulted does not carry to its conclusion (wirszubski1989:1479, 1482).
not_established: Wirszubski's completed argument about the thesis's referent (beyond the opening sentence quoted at wirszubski1989:1482) is not established by the material consulted.
Scholem's discussion of soul-emanation to which Farmer refers (farmer1998:17661) has not itself been opened for this entry.
not established by the sources consulted
